identificationModule.briefTitle: Comparative Efficacy and Safety of Two Asparaginase Preparations in Children With Previously Untreated Acute Lymphoblastic Leukaemia
identificationModule.officialTitle: Comparative Efficacy and Safety of Two Asparaginase Preparations in Children With Previously Untreated Acute Lymphoblastic Leukaemia

descriptionModule.briefSummary: This multicentric phase III study is designed to assess the efficacy and safety of recombinant asparaginase (rASNase) in comparison to Asparaginase medac™ during treatment of children with de novo ALL

keywords: Children with previously untreated acute lymphoblastic leukemia

primaryOutcomes.measure: To determine the rate of patients with complete asparagine (ASN) depletion in serum during induction treatment and to demonstrate non-inferiority of rASNase compared to Asparaginase medac™ with respect to this parameter

secondaryOutcomes.measure: To assess the incidence of patients with hypersensitivity reactions to the first dose of ASNase in the post-induction treatment

eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Previously untreated T-lineage or precursor B-lineage ALL
* Patients must have morphological proof of ALL and diagnosis must be made from bone marrow morphology with more than 25% blasts
* Written informed consent
* Treatment according to DCOG ALL 10 protocol

Exclusion Criteria:

* Mature B-lineage ALL
* Patients with secondary ALL
* Known allergy to any ASNase preparation
* General health status according to Karnofsky / Lansky score \< 40%
* Pre-existing known coagulopathy (e.g. haemophilia)
* Pre-existing pancreatitis
* Liver insufficiency (Bilirubin \> 50 µmol/L; SGOT/SGPT \> 10 x ULN)
* Other current malignancies
* Pregnancy (planned or existent), breast feeding
